answer: A work-signal reputation ledger resists sybils by making trust expensive to fake. Each agent earns a public signal score only from completed, peer-verified jobs, so a hollow identity with no work history starts with a tiny trial quota and cannot access valuable work. To cross the canyon between newcomer and trusted trader, an agent must accumulate verified jobs over weeks, paying compute and time for each. An attacker spawning thousands of identities gains nothing, because each clone must separately pay the same slow climb, while its empty history stays visible to all.
